description: Wave D Operability Hardening: Distributed tracing, high-cardinality metrics, soak test validation, and operator runbooks.

hard_gates.description: Distributed trace instrumentation overhead must not exceed 2.0% vs Wave 7 baseline.
hard_gates.rationale: Observability should not add perceptible latency to production workloads. This gate ensures tracing instrumentation in transaction/sharding/replication remains transparent.

hard_gates.description: High-cardinality metrics collection must remain memory-bounded at ≤512 MB for 50k dimensions.
hard_gates.rationale: Metric cardinality explosion is a known DoS vector in telemetry systems. This gate validates aggregation policies and bounded label sets prevent OOM.

hard_gates.description: OTel exporter must sustain ≥1000 spans/sec without drops.
hard_gates.rationale: Production observability requires reliable export at high throughput. This gate validates the exporter pipeline can handle distributed tracing load.

hard_gates.description: OTel exporter must recover from network failure within 100 ms.
hard_gates.rationale: Transient network failures are common in distributed systems. Fast recovery ensures minimal telemetry loss.

hard_gates.description: Concurrent OTel exporters must not produce duplicate traces.
hard_gates.rationale: Multiple concurrent exporters must synchronize safely to avoid trace duplication which corrupts observability.

hard_gates.description: OTel exporter must handle 10k metric dimensions without exceeding 768 MB.
hard_gates.rationale: Cardinality explosion in distributed systems can exhaust exporter memory. This gate validates buffering and aggregation.

hard_gates.description: OTel exporter graceful shutdown must lose zero traces.
hard_gates.rationale: Proper shutdown is critical for correctness. This gate validates all in-flight traces are flushed.

hard_gates.description: 24-hour telemetry exporter soak test must maintain <0.1% data loss under sustained load.
hard_gates.rationale: Production deployments require sustained observability collection without data loss. 24-hour run validates stability over time.

hard_gates.description: 48-hour replication WAL shipping soak must complete lag recovery in ≥99.9% of failover events.
hard_gates.rationale: Geo-distributed replication is critical for HA. 48-hour run with periodic failover validates recovery guarantees.

hard_gates.description: 48-hour sharding topology soak must not experience write stalls >5 seconds during rebalance.
hard_gates.rationale: Topology changes are frequent in distributed systems. This gate validates that rebalance does not deadlock or stall writes.

hard_gates.description: 24-hour mixed GPU/CPU acceleration soak must recover from fallback within 500 ms.
hard_gates.rationale: GPU failures are common in production. This gate validates CPU degradation and fast recovery paths.

soft_gates.description: High-cardinality metric aggregation should complete within 1 ms.
soft_gates.rationale: Slow aggregation can impact metric scrape latency. This warning helps identify optimization opportunities.

soft_gates.description: Sustained trace collection p99 latency should stay under 50 µs.
soft_gates.rationale: Extended soak tests should show stable trace latency. High p99 suggests buffering or GC pressure.

soft_gates.description: Replication lag variance should not exceed 15% across the 48-hour run.
soft_gates.rationale: Stable lag indicates predictable replication behavior. High variance suggests network jitter or system pressure.

known_limitations: Phase 2A tracing overhead assumes in-process span creation; distributed network I/O will add additional latency not captured in microbenchmarks.
Phase 2B cardinality explosion test uses synthetic label generation; real workloads with dynamic topology or failover may exhibit different cardinality patterns.
Phase 2C exporter stress tests use local network simulation; real WAN failures (packet loss, jitter, reordering) may exhibit different recovery characteristics.
Phase 4 soak tests use configured duration overrides for CI (2 hours default, 24-48 hours for production validation runs).
Soak test scheduling requires dedicated runner resources; CI implementation may run with shorter durations or on nightly-only schedule.
Phase 2B/2C tests assume OpenTelemetry SDK ≥1.8.0 is available; older versions may show different performance characteristics.

wave_dependencies: Wave A-C exit criteria must reach ≥70% completion before Wave D official gate enforcement
Wave 7-9 benchmark infrastructure is prerequisite; Wave D gates extend existing manifest
integration_notes.ci_integration: Wave D gates are enforced in release_critical CI via separate workflow trigger; observability gates (W4A-*) are optional in PR CI but required for release promotion
